summary: This is not your shared-liberty 10kKO. White's capture at A18 threatens to win at once from the start, and Black must fill A14 and C18 before its own capture threatens anything; with best play Black needs three threats more than White. Read as Black's approach ko, Black plays A14 with its move and the leaf is an A-1 form: A-1KO-, strictly A-1KO-2, because White's F19 or D19 is worth one more threat than taking at once. besogo grades any A-1 form exactly like your 10kKO. Read as the solver reads it, White plays F19, Black completes A14 and C18 before White takes, and the ko is a direct KO-3, which grades better for Black than 10kKO. Which reading is right is the open choice between the approach form and the counted form.
variations: 1) A14 F19 C18 A18 (the principal line): a direct ko in which Black, to move, fails with two threats more and wins with three, in both areas. 2) A14 A18 (White takes at once): Black needs only two (its best reply is F19). 3) A14 pass F19 C18 G19 A18 A19! A13 A18 A16 A18: if White plays elsewhere after A14, Black needs only one threat (it ends in the bulky-five sacrifice). 4) pass A18, then Black elsewhere once: White wins against six Black threats (A16 then C18 or A19), so White's capture threatens from the start, in both areas. 5) pass A18 A19!, then White elsewhere: Black cannot win, so its capture is not direct. After A14 A18 A19! Black needs two free moves (C18, D19). 6) F19 D19 ...: Black's other first move that keeps the count 3. 7) Old end rule: F19 D19 A14 A18 A19! F18 G19 A18 A19! A13 B13 A18 pass F17 A19 pass A18 pass pass. This line ends with Black's five corner stones and White's group sharing only A16 and C18, a seki. The old rule scored it as a kill (count 2); the end playout does not (count 3).

(1) Narrow leaf table, end playout: s1 W, s2 W, s3 B. Old end rule: s1 W, s2 B. Wider area: undecided at 2.4M in both rules. (2) leaf+A14 F19 C18 A18: s2 W, s3 B in the narrow and the wider area. (3) leaf+pass A18 with one forced Black pass: White wins 0 against 6 (narrow and wide). leaf+pass A18 A19! with one forced White pass: White wins. leaf+A14 A18 A19!: one forced pass, White wins; two, Black wins. leaf+A14 F19 C18 A18 A19! with one forced White pass: Black wins (narrow and wide). leaf+A14 F19 C18 A18 with one forced Black pass: White wins. (4) Black's first moves at s3: A14 and F19 win; A16, A18, C18, A13 and pass lose. After A14, White's moves at s2: D19 and F19 keep White's win; A18, A16, C18, A13 and pass lose. leaf+A14 A18: s0 W, s1 W, s2 B. leaf+A14 with one forced White pass: s0 W, s1 B. leaf+A14 F19: s2 W, s3 B. leaf+A14 A18 with one or two forced Black passes: White wins (W A19 or C18 then A16). (5) Walk of the old-end line: after B F19 W D19 the old end gives Black the win at s2 and the end playout gives White; the line's end position is the shared-liberty seki.
checker_part: KO-3 rests on D2. The first take is White's A18 on the principal line, after B A14, W F19, B C18, and the checker reads those moves as preparation, so both captures are direct (n_S = n_O = 0) and e = -d = -3. Under the approach form this is the part that changes: A14 and C18 are Black's approaches, White's capture threatens from the start, and the label is an A-1 form with White taking first. The local threat F18 (answered at F17) touches the area wall, but the direct ko's count of 3 holds in both areas, so the count itself is sound. The old end rule's count of 2 comes from scoring a seki as a kill.
depends_on: The research report's open approach-label decision: the approach form or the counted form for the same count (also question 4, the structure or the count). Approach form: A14 and C18 are Black's approaches, Black plays the first with its move, and White takes first, so the label is A-1KO-, strictly A-1KO-2 with the count 3. besogo ranks every A-1 form equal to 10kKO in a KILL problem, so the tree's S[10kKO] grades the same; only its notation is off. Counted form (the checker's D2, moves before the first take are preparation): KO-3, which besogo ranks above 10kKO for Black, so S[10kKO] would be a site error that changes the grading.
